model: Regulated utility dividend (FCFE) stream capitalised at cost of equity, exit on year-10 earnings (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E total revenues: 9M 2026 actual 18,297 (10-Q Q3 2026 line 16479) plus Q4 2026E ~5,850 (Q4 2025 was 5,315; 9M 2026 grew 10.5% YoY). FY2025 actual was 21,876.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average Q3 2026 (10-Q line 16502: 550,103,235); cover-page basic count 544,526,330 at 2026-10-28. Held FLAT: the operating-EPS guidance the earnings path is built from is already net of the equity AEP will issue to fund the $100B plan (ATM program up to $3.5B filed Nov 2025, forward sale agreements, Note 12). Compounding the count on top of per-share guidance would charge dilution twice.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO deliberately. The flow being discounted is dividends to AEP common, which is after interest expense (9M 2026: 1,743) and after NCI (9M 2026: 94). Deducting the $54.4B of debt again would double-count it. Actual 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet (10-Q lines 16658-16668, 16604-16606): short-term debt 1,875 + long-term debt due within one year 2,677 + long-term debt 49,864 = total debt 54,416; cash 418, restricted cash 89, other temporary investments 252; AEP common equity 32,775; noncontrolling interests ~1,268.
inputs.last_fcf_note: On this route last_fcf is the FY0 (FY2026E) dividend stream to common: $3.82 declared per share in 2026 (0.95 x3 + 0.97, Oct-2026 raise) x 550.1M shares. GAAP free cash flow is structurally negative and is NOT the valuation base: FY2025 OCF 6,944 minus construction expenditures 8,453 = -1,509; 9M 2026 OCF 5,767 minus construction 9,107 = -3,340. See inputs.notes for why.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement add-back $53M (0.24% of revenue; core_metrics stock_based_comp). Already expensed inside GAAP and operating earnings, so the dividend stream is post-SBC; it is NOT deducted a second time. sbc_pct_path is 0 and house = street (band collapses).
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field carries the COST OF EQUITY (8.0%), because the discounted flow is post-interest dividends to common. Build: 10-year US Treasury 4.86% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-06) + utility beta 0.55-0.65 x equity risk premium 5.0-5.5% = 7.6-8.4%; 8.0% taken. Cross-check: AEP trades ~2.1x book (price / 59.6 BVPS) on allowed ROEs of ~9.5-10%, which with 4-5% growth implies a market cost of equity of ~7%; 8.0% is deliberately above that. Same rate in all three scenarios so risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial (interest on lease liabilities ~$10-12M/yr, FY2025 10-K line 31740); inside operating earnings, no separate charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only: the earnings path is operating earnings attributable to AEP common, after the 19.9% Midwest Transmission Holdings NCI sold to KKR/PSP in June 2025 ($2.78B net proceeds). No further NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. AEP is a rate-regulated electric utility: earnings = allowed ROE x equity layer of rate base, and growth comes from capex that regulators add to rate base. The routing table in .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md has no utility row; the owner-FCF DCF is wrong here because reported FCF is structurally negative (FY2021-FY2025: -1,820 / -1,384 / -2,366 / -827 / -1,509; 9M 2026: -3,340) while the capex that drives it earns a regulated return above the cost of capital. Per the skill's principle ('discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues'), the model follows the GPT.AX/GMG.AX precedent of a post-interest stream at cost of equity with net debt at zero. The stream is DIVIDENDS to common (the cash equity holders actually receive), not earnings: with a ~59-62% payout, capitalising earnings would count the retained 40% twice (once as a flow, once via the growth it funds). The terminal value is Gordon on year-10 dividends, which at 8.0%/3.5% equals ~23x dividends or ~14x year-10 earnings, inside the utility sector's long-run 14-17x P/E range. ENGINE MAPPING (read the sliders this way): 'revenue' = total revenues; 'EBITDA margin' = PRE-TAX earnings attributable to common as % of revenue (post-interest, post-NCI); 'cash tax rate' = effective tax rate (FY2025 3.5%, 9M 2026 7.3%; path rises to 15% as OBBBA phases out PTCs/ITCs and excess-ADIT amortisation fades); 'capex' = RETAINED EARNINGS reinvested in rate base (earnings x (1 - payout)); SBC, D&A and working capital are zero so that FCF = dividends to common. FY0 is FY2026E (9M reported; guidance 'at or above the high end of $6.25-$6.55' -> $6.50 operating EPS, $3.82 DPS). Anchors: operating EPS 9M 2026 $5.19 (2,849 / 549.3M, 10-Q line 15166) vs 9M 2025 $4.76; Q3 2026 $2.21. FY2025 GAAP EPS $6.66 diluted (3,580 / 537.5M) includes +$762M of NOLC / excess-ADIT remeasurement one-offs (10-K lines 23445-23470), so GAAP history overstates the run-rate; the 9-11% growth algorithm is off the 2026 operating midpoint.
inputs.regulatory_anchors: 2027 operating EPS guidance $6.75-$7.05; 2028 $7.40-$7.70; 9-11% annual growth 2027-2031; capital plan $100B 2027-2031 ($37B transmission, $36B generation, $22B distribution); rate base CAGR 13%+ to ~$162B by 2031; 84 GW incremental contracted load by 2031; dividend payout target 60-70%.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management 2027-2031 operating EPS growth algorithm 9-11% (Q3 2026 release), haircut to 9.5% for regulatory lag; this is a forward guided rate, not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: GAAP EPS 3-yr CAGR (14.1%) is inflated by ~$762M of FY2025 NOLC/excess-ADIT one-offs; on operating EPS (FY2022 ~$5.09 -> FY2025 ~$5.95) the 3-yr CAGR is ~5.3%, below the equity CAGR. FCF CAGRs are null: reported FCF is negative in every year FY2021-FY2025 (capex > OCF by design in a rate-base build), so a CAGR is undefined.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2022 19,639.5 -> FY2025 21,876 (3y); FY2020 14,918.5 -> FY2025 (5y). GAAP diluted EPS FY2022 4.51 / FY2020 4.44 -> FY2025 6.70. Common equity FY2022 24,123 -> FY2025 31,138 (3y); FY2020 20,774.5 -> FY2025 31,138 (5y; ex the 1,080 NCI created June 2025). DPS FY2020 2.84 -> FY2025 3.74. Equity CAGR is the primary growth proxy per house rules; the forward guided rate is used because the capital plan has tripled the historical growth rate.

base.narrative: Operating EPS 6.50 (FY2026E) -> 6.90 (2027 midpoint) -> 7.55 (2028 midpoint) -> +9.5%/yr 2029-2031 (slight haircut to the 9-11% algorithm) -> fades 8/7/6/5/4.5% to 2036 as the plan rolls off and affordability caps rate growth; EPS 13.32 in 2036. Payout 59% rising to 62%. Terminal 3.5% = retention 38% x allowed ROE ~9.5%. Cap 30x dividends (~18x P/E) does not bind; Gordon gives ~23x dividends / ~14x earnings.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax earnings attributable to common / revenue = net margin / (1 - tax). FY2026E net margin 14.81% -> 15.5% by 2036.
base.capex_note: Retained earnings (earnings x (1 - payout)) as % of revenue; the equity AEP ploughs into rate base.

bull.narrative: Operating EPS at the top of guidance: 7.05 (2027), 7.80 (2028), then 11%/yr through 2031 as the 84 GW of contracted load connects on schedule and the plan is raised again; fade 9.5/8.5/7/6/5% to 2036 (EPS 15.09). Terminal 4.0% (data-center-driven load growth keeps rate base compounding above GDP); the 30x cap would bind only below ~7.5% CoE.

bear.narrative: 2027 at the low end (6.75), 2028 below the range (7.25) as rate-case lag and an Ohio/Texas affordability backlash bite, then 6-7% growth 2029-2031 (the pre-2025 algorithm) as a slice of the contracted data-center load slips or cancels and the plan is trimmed; fade to 3% by 2036 (EPS 10.65). Payout drifts up to 65% as reinvestment need falls; effective tax rises faster (17%) as credits phase out. Terminal 2.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: AEP delivers roughly the midpoint of its 2027 ($6.75-7.05) and 2028 ($7.40-7.70) operating EPS guidance and then compounds at ~9.5% through 2031 off the $100B capital plan, a touch under the 9-11% algorithm to allow for regulatory lag across 11 state commissions plus FERC. The 13%+ rate-base CAGR converts to ~9.5% EPS growth because the plan is part-funded with new equity (already inside the per-share guidance) and interest costs rise with the debt stack. The dividend grows with earnings at a 59-62% payout. After 2031 growth fades toward 4.5% as the large-load wave is absorbed and affordability pressure caps rate increases; the terminal 3.5% is the sustainable growth implied by 38% retention at a ~9.5% allowed ROE.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 84 GW of contracted incremental load connects on or ahead of schedule under take-or-pay tariffs, the capital plan is raised a fourth time, FERC transmission formula rates and PJM/SPP competitive awards keep the Transmission Holdco compounding, and AEP earns the top of its ranges (7.05 / 7.80) then 11% a year through 2031. Equity is raised at a premium to book, so dilution is modest and EPS reaches ~$15 by 2036. Interest rates ease, which this model does not credit via a lower cost of equity (risk charged once) but which would push the market multiple above the ~14x terminal P/E embedded here.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI/data-center capex cycle decelerates and a meaningful slice of contracted load is deferred or cancelled; take-or-pay protections limit stranded cost but the plan is trimmed and growth reverts to the pre-2025 6-7% algorithm. Consumer-advocate pushback in Ohio and Texas produces lower allowed ROEs and slower recovery, coal retirement and EPA compliance costs are partly disallowed, and higher-for-longer rates raise financing costs on a $54B debt stack. EPS still grows (regulated utilities rarely shrink) but only to ~$10.65 by 2036, the payout drifts up toward 65% and the effective tax rate rises faster as PTCs/ITCs phase out.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bull weight is cut because the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once: hyperscaler load arriving on schedule, constructive outcomes across 11 state commissions plus FERC, and benign financing conditions for $100B of capex. Bear weight is raised because the growth algorithm is now explicitly levered to one demand source (AI data centers) and management itself cautions in filings that the contracted load may not materialise or may arrive at a different pace; there is no solvency risk, so the bear is a growth and ROE downgrade, not distress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a stream of allowed returns on an ever-growing rate base; the value to a shareholder is the dividends that stream funds plus what the market will pay for the earnings power at the end of the horizon. This model discounts dividends to common at an 8% cost of equity (10-year Treasury 4.86% plus a utility-beta risk premium) and exits on year-10 earnings via Gordon growth, which lands at ~14x P/E. Debt is not deducted because the stream is already after interest. Negative reported FCF is a feature of the rate-base build, not a warning sign, and is not used. The three scenarios bracket the guidance ranges and the 9-11% algorithm; the cost of equity is held constant across them so that risk is charged once, through the weights.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: a long-duration dividend stream is acutely rate-sensitive; each 50bp on the discount rate moves the base value by roughly 10-12%. The 10-year Treasury at 4.86% is the single most important external input.
Data-center load durability: the 9-11% algorithm rests on 84 GW of contracted incremental load; cancellations or deferral revert growth to 6-7% (the bear case).
Regulatory outcomes across 11 states plus FERC: allowed ROE cuts, disallowances or slower recovery mechanisms reduce the conversion of rate-base growth to EPS growth.
Equity funding: the per-share guidance assumes equity is raised at prices near today's; a sharp de-rating would force more dilutive issuance than guided (not modelled separately).
Tax: the effective rate is assumed to rise from ~7% to 15% as credits phase out; faster normalisation or CAMT exposure lowers the net margin path.
Coal fleet (~10 GW) retirement and EPA compliance: write-downs and securitisation at below-allowed returns drag earnings.
